About the role
 The Data Analyst Assistant role is central to our current engagement with a Dubai-based investment firm that requires precise data handling and clear visualization. This position provides the quantitative groundwork that allows our principals to form a view on complex corporate governance and strategy questions. We need an assistant who can organize messy data sets into logical structures that reveal the health and performance of a holding company.

About Arabian Private Holdings
 Arabian Private Holdings was founded on the principle that many critical business problems do not fit the traditional large-firm consulting model. A board facing a succession question or a family group weighing a capital injection does not need a team of twelve associates and a hundred-page methodology deck. They need experienced partners who can sit with a problem, form a rigorous view, and defend it. We take on a limited number of mandates to ensure that every client receives direct attention from the principals who are actually accountable for the outcome. Our work covers corporate strategy, governance, and operating model efficiency for some of the most significant family groups, listed corporations, and government entities in the region. We focus on clarity over complexity. We operate as a remote firm, choosing to prioritize the quality of our analysis and the strength of our relationships over traditional office overhead or aggressive growth targets.

What you will do
  • Collect and organize financial and operational data from various portfolio companies for a Dubai-based investment.
  • Clean and validate data sets to ensure accuracy before they are used in client presentations.
  • Build simple, effective spreadsheets that track performance indicators for large holding companies.
  • Assist in drafting reports that translate numbers into clear written arguments for our principals.
  • Monitor industry trends and perform basic market research to support ongoing strategic mandates.
  • Maintain internal records to ensure that historical client data is easily accessible and correctly categorized.
  • Prepare charts and graphs that simplify complex financial structures for board-level reviews.
  • Support the audit of corporate governance documents by cross-referencing quantitative findings with qualitative reports.


What we are looking for
  • A clear understanding of basic statistics and a logical approach to problem-solving.
  • Proficiency in spreadsheet software with an ability to manage large amounts of information without errors.
  • Strong written skills and the ability to explain what a set of numbers means in plain English.
  • Curiosity about how large corporations and family groups operate in different sectors.
  • Precision in your work, where you check your own calculations before submitting them for review.
  • A degree or ongoing studies in a quantitative field such as economics, finance, or mathematics.


How we work
 We operate as a fully remote firm, which means we rely on clear documentation and asynchronous communication. Because our work involves sensitive mandates for high-profile clients, we maintain a high standard of professional conduct and data security. You will work closely with a principal who provides direct mentorship and expects you to form your own view on the data you analyze. We do not value long hours for the sake of appearances. Instead, we focus on the rigor of the output and the clarity of the logic. This remote model allows us to hire individuals based on their intellectual capability rather than their physical location, ensuring we can provide the best possible advice to our clients.

What the role offers
  • A paid entry-level position with a competitive compensation package for the current market.
  • Direct exposure to high-level corporate strategy and governance mandates.
  • Mentorship from experienced principals who have managed some of the largest holding companies in the region.
  • The flexibility of a permanent, full-time role that is entirely remote.
  • Practical experience in forming a rigorous view on business performance and portfolio health.

Location: UK or Canada (Atlantic Time Zone only)

Meet The Guru

Resource Guru is a blissfully simple scheduling tool that helps busy teams stay on track.

We boost efficiency, improve resource utilisation, and increase project profitability - while promoting a healthy work/life balance.

Weâre proud to be one of the leaders in our category, trusted by customers in over 100 countries - including top creative agencies like Publicis, TBWA, Grey, BBH, and M&C Saatchi, as well as household names like NASA, Accenture, CNN, Kraft Heinz, and the NHS. They rely on Resource Guru to manage one of their most valuable assets - their peopleâs time.

Weâre a small, fully remote team based across the UK and Europe. We collaborate mainly via Slack, with occasional meetups to connect, plan, and celebrate. See if this is the right place for you.

â­ï¸ The role

Weâre looking for a Customer Support Specialist to join our team.

As more teams use Resource Guru and as we continue to support larger, more complex customers we want to make sure every customer receives fast, clear, thoughtful and genuinely helpful support.

This role is primarily about helping customers by email, understanding their questions, troubleshooting issues, and making sure they get the best possible experience from Resource Guru.

Youâll work closely with Dana, our Senior Customer Support Specialist, and collaborate with our product and engineering teams when customer questions, bugs or feature requests need to be investigated further. We see Customer Support as a core part of building a great product, so youâll work closely with the rest of the team to help improve Resource Guru, not just answer support tickets.

This is a great role for someone with some experience in SaaS or online customer support who wants to keep developing their technical, communication and customer-facing skills in a friendly, remote-first team.

What Youâll Be Doing

Learning Resource Guru inside out

  • In your first few months, you'll get to know Resource Guru inside out - how customers use the product, what common questions come up, and how to guide people towards the right answer.

Responding to customer questions

  • Help customers with day-to-day support questions, including product usage, account setup, billing enquiries, troubleshooting and general "how do Iâ¦?" queries.
  • Most support is handled by email, though you may occasionally join a phone or video call when that would help resolve something more quickly.

Troubleshooting problems

  • Investigate customer issues carefully and methodically - asking the right follow-up questions, checking account settings, trying to reproduce a problem, looking for browser-related issues, or escalating a bug to engineering with clear notes.

Working with the wider team

  • Work closely with Dana and the wider Resource Guru team to understand customer questions, resolve issues, and make sure useful feedback is shared with Product and Engineering.
  • Help create clear internal reports when customers report bugs or technical issues, and tag/categorise feature feedback so the team understands what customers need.

Improving our help content

  • Help keep the Help Centre useful and up to date - updating existing articles, writing new ones, recording simple walkthroughs, or suggesting improvements when you notice customers asking the same questions repeatedly.

Using our support tools

  • Use tools such as Front, Recurly, Customer.io, HubSpot and other internal systems to manage customer conversations, billing questions and account information. We don't expect you to know all of these already, but you should be comfortable learning new software quickly.

Helping customers feel looked after

  • A big part of this role is making sure customers feel heard, understood and helped. We care about support that is accurate and efficient, but also warm, human and thoughtful.

What Weâre Looking ForEssential experience

  • 1-3 yearsâ experience in online customer support, ideally for a B2B SaaS or similar software company
  • Excellent written and spoken English and the ability to explain things clearly, simply and warmly
  • A calm, patient and empathetic approach to helping customers
  • Good attention to detail, especially when dealing with billing, account or technical questions
  • A practical approach to troubleshooting and problem-solving
  • Confidence learning new software tools and understanding how web-based products work
  • Some familiarity with basic technical concepts such as browsers, cache, cookies, internet connection issues and permissions
  • The ability to work independently in a remote team and manage your time well
  • A collaborative and conscientious attitude and willingness to share useful customer feedback with product, engineering and the wider team
  • Comfort with asynchronous communication and keeping written conversations clear, concise and on track

You donât need to be a developer, but you should be curious about technology and comfortable investigating how things work.

Bonus (not required)

It would be a bonus if you have experience with any of the following:

  • Supporting a SaaS product
  • Helping customers with billing, subscriptions or invoices
  • Writing Help Centre articles or customer-facing guides
  • Using support tools such as Front, Intercom, Zendesk, HubSpot or similar
  • Working in a fully remote team
  • Recording short customer help videos or walkthroughs
  • Supporting customers across multiple time zones, especially APAC-friendly hours
  • Comfortable using AI tools to improve the quality and efficiency of your work

Working Hours

This is a remote role, for people based in either the UK or Canada (Atlantic Time Zone only). Youâll also need regular overlap with the UK team for training, collaboration and handovers.

The exact working pattern will depend on your location and the coverage we agree, but you should be clear in your application about where youâre based and what working hours you would expect to keep.

â Our Hiring Process

  • Meet with Imogen (Talent/People Ops): 25-30m video call. Imogen will tell you a bit more about what itâs like to be on Team Guru. Please come prepared with any questions about our ways of working or team structure.
  • Meet with Dana (Customer Support): 60m video call. Dana will talk with you about your previous support experience, your communication style, your technical troubleshooting skills, and any experience you have with billing or invoice-related enquiries.
  • Meet with Percy (cofounder): 30m video call. This will follow a typical interview format with an opportunity for you to ask questions and learn more about the role.
  • Reference checks
  • Offer! â¨

â­ï¸ What Weâre Offering

  • A great salary
  • Stock options
  • Work from anywhere you like - co-working space will be provided if necessary
  • 30 days paid holiday + Dec 24 - Jan 1 company holiday
  • Birthday off + house move day off
  • Flexible hours
  • Annual training and conference allowance - Â£3,000
  • A home office equipment contribution upon joining (then every 3 years) - Â£1,000

jobs.title: Senior OSINT Data Analyst
jobs.description:
Datenna is a fast-growing tech scale-up combining cutting-edge OSINT and AI technologies to provide governments with critical insights into China's techno-economic landscape. Our platform transforms open-source intelligence into actionable insights through advanced data processing and analysis.


The Role: As Senior OSINT Data Analyst you will sit at the core of Datenna’s product operations and act as a domain authority for our data. You will define which foreign-language sources we collect for each region we cover, set and defend the standards that data is held to, and turn complex registry, procurement, and patent material into structured, platform-ready intelligence. You will own major areas of coverage end to end, guide the analysts around you, and be a trusted voice in product decisions. 

 

Your mission at Datenna:

Analysis and data intelligence 

  • Apply deep regional domain knowledge to develop products that identify, map, and classify entities across corporate, academic, defence-industrial, and innovation landscapes, with a focus on state-military-commercial integration, dual-use technologies, state ownership, and technology transfer.

  • Use pattern-recognition skills to connect corporate, state, and military actors, including opaque ownership structures and intermediaries, and generate structured intelligence that feeds directly into Datenna’s platform.

  • Make and defend analytical judgements on entity risk labelling, ownership mapping, and procurement tracking, prioritising platform-ready outputs over long-form research deliverables.

Data Collection, quality and lifecycle management

  • Define and own data collection workstreams end to end: identifying, evaluating, and extracting structured information from non-English sources including corporate registries, procurement portals, patent databases, academic repositories, and state media.

  • Manage data across its full lifecycle, from initial acquisition and parsing through cleaning, enrichment, validation, and delivery into Datenna’s platform, maintaining rigorous standards so that every data point is traceable, accurate, and defensible.

  • Work closely with the Data Lead to set and continuously refine data quality benchmarks, turning observations from collection and testing work into improvements to automated pipelines.


Product development

  • Play a leading role in Datenna’s data-driven product development cycle, contributing regional domain expertise to the design, testing, and refinement of new platform features and data products.

  • Shape how Datenna’s proprietary risk labelling systems evolve, drawing on hands-on OSINT experience to identify edge cases and improve classification accuracy.

  • Map gaps in Datenna’s data coverage against what customers need, and make the case for the sources, methods, and investment required to close them, including the extension of our approach to new regions.


Coordination and collaboration

  • Coordinate between data researchers and software developers to support smooth data processing pipelines, translating analytical requirements into clear technical specifications.

  • Set the methodological standard for OSINT work as the team grows: reviewing outputs, mentoring junior and medior researchers on OSINT tradecraft, and ensuring work meets Datenna’s data quality standards.


What makes you a great candidate:

  • 8-10 years of hands-on OSINT experience, including direct collection, verification, and analysis from non-English open sources such as corporate registries, government procurement portals, patent databases, academic repositories, and state media.

  • Demonstrable experience contributing to data-driven product development, whether through structured dataset creation, analytical input into software features, or validation of intelligence platform outputs.

  • Reading proficiency in Chinese at minimum HSK 4 level or equivalent, together with the ability to independently source, interrogate, and extract structured data from foreign-language materials. Working proficiency in Russian is preferred. 

  • Strong knowledge of at least one region’s corporate sector, innovation ecosystem, defence-industrial base, industrial policy, and the intersection of state, military, and commercial actors, with the ability to identify entity-level connections across Datenna’s key domains and to learn new jurisdictions quickly.

  • Proficiency in both qualitative and quantitative research methods, with experience producing analytical outputs for non-specialist audiences and presenting findings to customers or senior stakeholders.

  • Familiarity with data analysis tools such as Python, R, or SQL, and comfort working with large structured datasets and contributing to data pipelines. Experience with name-matching and transliteration at scale, for example Chinese or Cyrillic, is an advantage.

  • A postgraduate qualification in Area Studies, International Relations, Security Studies, or a related field is preferred.

*Please know that applicants may be subject to a screening process.*

AI is part of how we build

We use AI tools extensively to move faster and raise quality, and we focus our human attention on the work where judgment, creativity, and responsibility matter most. We expect every candidate to be comfortable using AI in their day-to-day work in a responsible manner and to continuously look for better ways to apply it.

  • Lead innovation in OSINT and AI technologies

  • Competitive compensation and benefits

  • Dynamic, international team environment

  • Significant growth opportunities in a scale-up

jobs.description:
Das erwartet dich bei uns:

  • Du arbeitest in Beratungs- und Softwareentwicklungsprojekten bei Kunden wie AXA, BMW, der Deutschen Bahn und ZDF

  • Du konzipierst, entwickelst und implementierst Softwarelösungen, in dem du AI-Methoden und Tools im gesamten Softwareentwicklungsprozess anwendest (z.B. LLMs, agentische Frameworks, Codegenerierung und Testautomatisierung)

  • Du wirkst in allen Disziplinen des Software-Engineerings mit und schreibst gut designten, testbaren und effizienten Code

  • Du nutzt bekannte Technologien, wie Java, JavaScript, Spring, Kotlin, Maven, Gradle, JUnit etc.

  • Beispielprojekte findest du unter Success-Stories

Das zeichnet dich aus:

  • Du hast einen Hochschulabschluss in Informatik oder in einer vergleichbaren Disziplin erfolgreich abgeschlossen

  • Du verfügst über tiefgehende und praktische Erfahrung in der professionellen Softwareentwicklung

  • Du arbeitest gern mit agilen Methoden wie Scrum oder Design Thinking

  • Du handelst proaktiv, pragmatisch und teamorientiert

  • Du sprichst fließend Deutsch (mindestens C1 Level) und sehr gut Englisch (mindestens B2)

Unser Angebot an dich:

  • Wertschätzung & Zusammenarbeit auf Augenhöhe​

  • 12 Weiterbildungstage pro Jahr​

  • Fachlicher Austausch & Wissenstransfer: 14 interne Communities & Netzwerke (z.B. ML, Green IT, Architektur, IoT)

  • Familienfreundliche Arbeitszeiten​ und hybrides Arbeiten mit Homeoffice-Anteil

  • Jobrad, Workation, Sabbatical, Kinderbetreuungszuschuss, Gesundheitsprogramme und vieles mehr

Das ist Accso:​

Accso ist Digitalpartner für anspruchsvolle Softwarelösungen nach Maß – mit AI Native Mindset. Wir verbinden exzellentes Engineering und Qualitätsbewusstsein mit pragmatischem KI-Einsatz, von der Konzeption über die Entwicklung bis hin zum Betrieb. Uns treibt eine klare Vision: die Welt ein Stück besser machen, indem wir gemeinsam mit unseren Kunden zukunftssichere Softwareentwicklung und messbaren Impact schaffen. Dabei steht der Mensch im Fokus – bei unseren Kunden genauso wie in unseren Teams. Wir arbeiten partnerschaftlich, lösungsorientiert, exzellenzgetrieben, mit offener Kommunikation auf Augenhöhe. In interdisziplinären Teams bringst du dich direkt beim Kunden ein – mit viel Gestaltungsspielraum, aktivem Wissenstransfer und einer Kultur, die Neugier, Verantwortung und Lernen fördert. Bei uns kannst du dich einbringen, wie du bist, moderne Technologien verantwortungsbewusst einsetzen und dich fachlich wie persönlich stetig weiterentwickeln. Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung.

Deine Bewerbung:

Es ist uns nicht so wichtig, dass du die Stellenanforderungen zu 100% erfüllst, sondern dass du unser Team mit deinen Talenten, deinem Wissen und deiner Art bereicherst und wir gemeinsam wachsen. ​

jobs.title: Senior Digital IC Design Engineer
jobs.description:
About The Role and Team

Quantum Motion is a fast-growing quantum computing scale-up based in London founded by internationally renowned researchers from UCL and Oxford University with over 40 years’ experience in developing qubits and quantum computing architectures. Bringing together state-of-the-art cryogenic facilities and an outstanding interdisciplinary team, we are developing quantum processors based on industrial-grade silicon chips, with the potential to radically transform computing power in areas such as materials modelling, medicine, artificial intelligence and more.


Our Team

Since 2021 our team has been listed every year in the “Top 100 Startups worth watching” in the EE Times in 2021 and 2022, and our technology breakthroughs have been featured in The Telegraph, BBC and the New Statesman. Our founders are internationally renowned researchers from UCL and Oxford University who have pioneered the development of qubits and quantum computing architectures. Our chairman is the co-founder of Cadence and Synopsys, the two leading companies in the area of Electronic Design Automation. We’re backed by a team of top-tier investors, and we have recently closed our Series C funding of $160 million.

We bring together the brightest quantum engineers, integrated circuit (IC) engineers, quantum computing theoreticians and software engineers to create a unique, world-leading team, working together closely to maximise our combined expertise. Our collaborative and interdisciplinary culture is an ideal fit for anyone who thrives in a cutting-edge research and development environment focused on tackling big challenges and contributing to the development of scalable quantum computers based on silicon technology.

This is a rare and exciting opportunity to be an employee at a scale-up shaping the future of quantum computing. There are vast opportunities for professional growth and to make an impact within the company.

Our team of 100+ is based across London, Oxford, San Sebastián and Sydney, with our primary hub in Islington (London).


Functions of the Role

This senior position operates at the critical intersection of sub-Kelvin sub-system electronics and quantum processor architectures, directly addressing the interconnect bottleneck in scalable quantum computing systems. The role spans the full digital IC design cycle—including initial microarchitecture specification, RTL development, Verilog-AMS co-simulation, physical implementation (PnR/CTS), low-power synthesis, static timing analysis (STA), and full tape-out signoff. The ultimate objective is the realization of ultra-low-power, high-density cryogenic control ICs tailored for fault-tolerant quantum computing scale-out.


  • Position Title:  Senior Digital Designer (Front-End & Back-End)

  • Domain Focus:  Ultra-Low-Power Cryogenic CMOS (Cryo-CMOS) Digital Control Sub-circuits

  • Design Scope:  Full Lifecycle (RTL Development, AMS Co-Simulation, Physical Implementation, Low-Power Synthesis, and Tape-Out Signoff)

  • Core Chip Architecture Target: Cryogenic digital logic blocks operating at sub-Kelvin regimes (<4.2 K), 


Experience - Essentials

  • Education: Master's degree or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Microelectronics, Computer Engineering, or related technical discipline.

  • Chip Design Experience: 5+ years of hands-on digital and mixed-signal IC design, demonstrating successful completion of at least 2 tape-outs on advanced semiconductor nodes 

  • Hardware Coding: Proficiency in Verilog and SystemVerilog for synthesizable RTL development and Verilog-AMS/SystemVerilog-Real-Math for mixed-signal co-simulation and testbench environments.

  • Design Tools: Proven proficiency with industry-standard EDA toolchains (e.g., Cadence Virtuoso/Innovus/Xcelium, Synopsys Design Compiler) for mixed-signal simulation, synthesis, and verification.

  • Physical Layout: Demonstrated capability in transforming RTL into GDSII/OASIS physical layouts, floorplanning, power grid synthesis, clock tree synthesis (CTS), multi-corner multi-mode static timing analysis (MCMM STA), and physical signoff (DRC/LVS/ERC).

  • Communication & Logic Design: Experience architecting high-speed serial interconnect protocols (e.g., custom SPI, AXI, SerDes) and complex finite-state machine (FSM) control logic.

  • Low Power & Thermal Management: Deep expertise in low-power dissipation techniques (clock gating, power gating, dynamic voltage scaling) within stringent thermal lift budgets of cryogenic cooling systems.


Experience - Desirable

  • Cryogenic CMOS Experience: Hands-on experience designing, modeling, or characterizing CMOS circuits at sub-4.2 K temperatures and understanding cryo-specific transistor behavior.
  • Mixed-Signal & AMS Interfaces: Direct integration of digital logic with precision analog/RF front-ends (ADCs, DACs, LNAs, AWGs) for qubit control and readout.
  • Quantum Architecture Awareness: Familiarity with quantum control interfaces, pulse generation, error correction, or cryogenic spin qubit electronics
  • Low-Power Verification & UPF/CPF: Proficiency in power-aware simulation using IEEE 1801 UPF/CPF, formal LEC, and power signoff tools (Voltus, PrimePower).
  • Advanced Process Nodes: Experience with sub-28nm nodes, with a strong preference for FD-SOI or FinFET technologies.
  • EDA Scripting & Automation: Strong scripting skills (TCL, Python) to automate synthesis, physical design, and verification flows.
  • DFT & Silicon Bring-Up: Practical knowledge of DFT insertion (Scan, MBIST) and post-silicon laboratory bring-up, testing, and debug.


Benefits

  • Be part of a creative, world-leading team
  • Competitive salary and share options scheme
  • Contributory pension scheme
  • Group private medical insurance scheme
  • Choose your own laptop/kit
  • Life Assurance
  • Cycle-to-work Scheme
  • Flexible working
  • Central London location


EEO Statement

Quantum Motion is committed to providing equal employment opportunity and does not discriminate based on age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, race, colour, religion, disability status, marital status, pregnancy, gender reassignment or any other protected characteristics covered by the Equality Act 2010.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager (f/m/x)
jobs.description:
Your Mission

This is a company built for growth, not comfort.

When you join exmox, you're stepping onto a global, highly competitive playing field, solving real problems in environments that push you beyond your comfort zone.

We build high-performing consumer products in one of the most competitive industries there is: mobile gaming, leading one of its largest innovations, a rewarded user engagement and acquisition platform that helps publishers acquire and retain players through rewarding experiences.

Senior Product Manager (f/m/x) isn't just about shipping features, it's about building products that perform. Product at exmox means understanding the bigger business picture, considering cross-functional impact across Engineering, Data, Marketing, and Operations, and turning strategy into product decisions that create real value, knowing every change you ship affects millions of users. At exmox, we're also embracing AI as part of how we work, not just what we build. We use AI tools to work smarter, cut down on repetitive tasks and spend our time where it actually moves the needle. If that mindset speaks to you, you'll fit right in.

If you're energized by dynamic markets, complex products, and the challenge of building products that perform at scale, we want to hear from you.

What You’ll Own:

  • Own one of exmox's highest-impact product domains end-to-end, shaping the reward economy through payout thresholds, tiering, bonuses, promotions, and other key levers that drive profitability.
  • Drive activation, retention, and long-term engagement through onboarding experiences, streaks, quests, progression systems, reactivation flows, and other lifecycle initiatives.
  • Take new growth opportunities from first hypothesis to go/no-go decision, across product, market expansion, partnerships, and distribution.
  • Lead a high-quality experimentation process by defining hypotheses, designing statistically sound A/B tests, interpreting results, and making data-driven product decisions.
  • Partner closely with your dedicated Data Analyst to uncover opportunities, validate assumptions, and continuously improve product performance.
  • Work with Engineering, Design, Commercial, User Acquisition, Customer Support, Fraud, and Leadership to align priorities and deliver impactful product improvements.
  • Represent your product domain directly to leadership, using data, customer insights, and business context to influence strategic decisions.

What Success Looks Like:

  • You take ownership quickly: Within your first months, you've become the trusted owner of a critical product domain, confidently driving priorities, making decisions, and reducing dependency on leadership.
  • Growth metrics measurably improve: Your product strategy and experimentation drive meaningful improvements in activation, retention, and long-term user profitability.
  • Product decisions are driven by data: Experiments, user insights, and product analytics provide clear evidence to prioritize opportunities, validate ideas, and confidently decide what to scale - or stop.
  • Cross-functional teams are aligned around outcomes: You partner closely with Engineering, Design, Data, Commercial, and User Acquisition to deliver product improvements that balance user value with business impact.
  • You turn ambitious ideas into scalable growth: Through structured experimentation, clear prioritization, and continuous optimization, you build product experiences that become repeatable growth levers for the business.
  • You outgrow the role: We are hiring for the ceiling, not just the opening. This role is scoped to grow - mentoring other product managers first, and leading a product team as we scale, if that is the direction you want to take.

What You Bring

  • Experienced: You bring 5+ years of Product Management experience in consumer-facing digital products, ideally within mobile apps, gaming, marketplaces, subscriptions, ad-tech, fintech, or other high-growth B2C businesses. You have owned consumer product at scale - hundreds of thousands of monthly active users or more.
  • Business-Oriented: You understand that product decisions are business decisions. You're comfortable balancing user needs, commercial objectives, and technical constraints to maximize long-term value.
  • Fluent in Incentives: You have a real feel for why people come back and what makes a reward feel worth the effort. You have designed incentive, reward or progression mechanics and calibrated them so they motivate without eroding margin.
  • Experimentation-Driven: You have extensive experience running A/B tests, defining hypotheses, interpreting data, and making evidence-based product decisions. Statistical thinking comes naturally to you.
  • Data-Literate: You're comfortable working with product metrics and collaborating closely with analysts to uncover insights, measure success, and prioritize opportunities.
  • Strategic & Hands-on: You enjoy defining product strategy while remaining deeply involved in execution - from writing specifications and refining solutions to reviewing experiment results and driving delivery.
  • Collaborative: You build strong partnerships across Product, Engineering, Design, Analytics, Marketing, Commercial, and Leadership, bringing people together around clear product goals.
  • Intellectually Honest: You're comfortable working in ambiguity, take ownership without waiting for direction, and thrive in fast-moving environments where priorities evolve quickly. You also kill your own ideas when the data says so - being wrong early is cheaper than being right late.

How We Win

  • Speed is the feature. Speed beats rocket science. We move fast, test fast, and multiply our pace with AI, because action creates information and small wins compound. A fast failure is a lesson we learn from, a slow one is a problem we can't afford.
  • Focus on the essential. Done is better than perfect. We stay focused on what actually moves us forward and protect people's time from anything that doesn't. We're direct in how we communicate too, no rambling, no unnecessary detail.
  • See it. Own it. Solve it. The first to see it is best placed to fix it. We're not a place for comfort, we're a place for doers. "Not my job" isn't in our vocabulary, if you spot something, you help make sure it gets solved.
  • Respect others. Trust multiplies. Respect is non-negotiable. We disagree with ideas, never with people. Trust here is built the same way it is anywhere, through consistency, a thank you, a moment of listening, and owning your mistakes.
  • Perks that help you focus on what matters. Transport subsidy, learning budget, wellness and gym, workation, bi-weekly team lunches, and more. The perks are great, but the real reason people join and stay is the challenge, the ownership, and the drive to win together.

Please note: this is not a remote only position, we offer you a flexible hybrid model here in Hamburg, Germany - working from home on Mondays & Fridays, coming to the office on Tuesday, Wednesday & Thursday!

jobs.title: Country Executive
jobs.description:
The finance function is broken. Everyone building for it is boring.

Fast-growing multi-entity companies get two options: duct-tape a Frankenstack, or surrender to a corporate ERP and its consultant army. Both are bad. Both are beatable. Beating them market by market is this job.

Light is the AI-native financial platform for modern companies. Fast to implement, intuitive to use, smarter every month. We call it organic software. Legora, Lovable, and Fuse Energy run on it. Product ships something worth shouting about every single week.

What we don't have is a single person on the ground in your country.


THIS IS NOT A COUNTRY MANAGER ROLE.

Most first-in-market hires get a quota, a deck, and a flight. They repeat the London pitch in a local accent and forward complaints to HQ. This is the opposite. This is a founding hire for someone who wants far more scope than their years of experience would get them anywhere else.

No entity. No local team. No local playbook. You are Light's first boots on the ground in your market, and within a year you should know that market's complexity - its rules, its buyers, its excuses - better than anyone else. It's not a leadership title. It's the seed of one. Do this right and there's a real path: stand up an entity, hire a team around you, move into product, or run the region as GM.


WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING.

  • Sitting across from finance leaders. Real conversations, not discovery calls off a script. You find out what they actually need - the thing behind the thing they asked for - and you come back with it written down clearly enough for engineers to build against.

  • Being the connective tissue. Customer, product, commercial. What you learn in-market changes how Light builds and how Light sells. You are the wire between them, and the wire has to carry current in both directions.

  • Owning the local rulebook. Compliance, regulation, filing, the specific ways finance is done badly in your country. You're the person in the room who genuinely knows this, and you make sure it shows up in the product and in the pitch.

  • Having a public point of view. Ideally you arrive with a finance background and an opinion on what "doing finance right" looks like here. Bring it into the market, into the roadmap, and into how every prospect sees Light. Relationships, events, brand presence - built from zero, by you.

  • Closing, with London behind you. Our sales team helps you manage and push deals over the line. You bring the market and customer understanding that makes those conversations land. They support you; they don't carry you and you don't carry it alone.

HOW WE'LL KEEP SCORE.

This isn't a pure revenue seat, but growing your country's ARR is the primary goal and you're tied directly to that number. A starting point will be set on what you're measured against on day one and you have to prove your worth.


WHAT WE'LL ASK FOR.

  • The thing you built from nothing. A company, a market, a GTM motion, a product. Something that existed because you hacked through a messy sale with no playbook. First question in the first call.

  • Credibility in front of a CFO. A finance background ideally, or enough substance that a finance leader takes you seriously the moment you walk in. You can't be the voice of the market without an ear for the buyer.

  • 2+ years as a founder or co-founder. Ex-founder or very early operator. We want the scar tissue.

  • 6+ years somewhere fast. High-growth tech, top-tier strategy consulting, investment banking, or similar. Or a body of work that makes the number irrelevant.

  • Structured thinking under mess. Exceptional analytical instincts, applied to markets nobody has mapped for you yet.

  • Fluency in your market's language and in English. Both, properly.

Extra credit: exposure to accounting, enterprise software, fintech or SaaS as a user, buyer or advisor; time spent presenting to senior finance stakeholders; an existing finance network in your market - or a demonstrated, unembarrassed intent to build one.


THE GOOD STUFF.

💸 Competitive salary plus potential stock options.
🏝 25 days annual leave plus public holidays where you're based.
🚀 A genuine chance to build a market from the ground up and grow with it.
🥳 Regular socials and company off-sites - the last one was in Italy.
🌍 Time with the team in London, Copenhagen, Munich, NY, Paris and wherever the action is.


HOW TO APPLY.

Show us who you are, not just your CV. Tell us what you built and what it did in numbers. Then answer the only question that matters: why this one? Anyone can say they want to work at a startup. A generic AI-written cover letter with no craft behind the prompt will be obvious - and is its own kind of answer.

If this reads as too much scope for one person: it is. That's the seat.

Light is an equal opportunity employer.

jobs.title: AI Support Engineer Lead
jobs.description:
About Dust

Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it.

With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done.

With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast.

We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50.

Summary

 

At Dust, we're building for a new kind of AI Operator: people who rethink and rebuild how their teams work around AI. Not “how can AI help us do this faster?” but “if AI existed from day one, would we even do this the same way?”

 

As our AI Support Engineering Lead, you'll own how Support is built and scaled at Dust. This is a deeply hands-on role. You'll take on the hardest customer issues when our agents fall short, but your job isn't simply to resolve them. You'll look for the pattern behind each issue and turn what you learn into better agents, automation, tooling, documentation, and product improvements. Over time, you'll help grow the team and shape how Support Engineering operates as Dust scales.

 

You'll define, ship, and continuously iterate on the systems that make this possible: AI agents, automation workflows, classification systems, knowledge systems, and tooling built on top of Dust itself. You'll dogfood the product harder than almost anyone at the company and set the standard for how the rest of the Support Engineering team does the same.

 

We're looking for someone who wants to lead from the work: technically strong, obsessed with building better systems, and excited to shape both the team and the function as we grow.

 

What you'll do

 

Build the AI systems that do the work

  • Set the technical direction for the support stack: what gets automated, in what order, and to what standard. You make the calls, not just the builds.

  • Design, ship, and maintain AI agents and automation workflows that reduce manual support load: think ticket classification, acknowledgment automation, response drafting, incident detection, and proactive user outreach.

  • Identify recurring categories of issues and engineer them out of existence through automation, documentation, prompt iteration, or product feedback.

  • Build and maintain tooling (MCP integrations, Dust agents, internal scripts) that increase the team's capacity without increasing headcount.

  • Define and own the "Support as a Product" backlog. You decide what goes on it, coach the team to execute it, and hold the bar on what shipped means.

 

Run support when the systems fall short

  • Hire, onboard, and develop the support engineers around you. You're not just resolving tickets and building systems, you're growing the people who will.

  • Set the standard for how complex issues get handled at Dust. You take the hardest tickets yourself. The team knows what good looks like because they've watched you do it.

  • Investigate complex issues across logs, code, and internal tooling to identify root causes and provide clear answers to customers.

  • Handle escalated cases with precise, accessible communication for both technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Systematically analyze agent-generated responses for inconsistencies and iterate on prompts, documentation, and tooling until human intervention is minimal.

 

Bridge customer pain to product improvements

  • Represent support at the engineering and product level. You synthesize signal, prioritize it, and push it through with enough context that it actually moves things, not just relays it.

  • Build strong working relationships with engineers and customer-facing teams to ensure efficient, high-context escalations.

  • Own the feedback loop end-to-end: when agents fail due to missing or incorrect information, close the gap across engineering, product, and documentation.

 

Requirements

Every candidate and employee's success is measured against the same 3 dimensions: Aptitude, Attitude and Agency.

 

Aptitude

  • Function-building experience: You've defined or significantly shaped a support engineering function before: built the operating model, set the standards, hired into the team, or rebuilt a broken process from scratch.

  • High technical aptitude: comfortable reading code, analyzing logs, navigating codebases, and troubleshooting distributed systems. You're not stopped by a stack trace.

  • AI fluency at builder level: track record of building custom agents, automations, or workflows using AI tools (Dust, Cursor, Claude Code, n8n, etc.); not just prompting.

  • Exceptional prioritization: You know what to solve immediately, what to automate, what to escalate, and, critically, what to delegate and to whom. You make these calls for yourself and for the team, fast and without second-guessing.

  • People leadership: You've coached and developed engineers and know how to set expectations, give direct feedback, and raise the performance of the people around you.

  • Bidirectional communication: can translate technical concepts to non-technical audiences and speak technical language fluently with engineers.

  • Build/Run mindset: You believe the best Support Engineering teams don't just resolve issues. They build systems that prevent those issues from recurring.

 

Attitude

  • Builder mentality: You instinctively automate repetitive work rather than accepting inefficient systems, and you hold your team to the same standard.

  • Resilience-empathy paradox: You can absorb customer frustration without taking it personally while still deeply caring about the user experience.

  • Leads by example: You're not above the queue. When something is hard, you take it.

  • Exceptional prioritization: You know what to solve immediately, what to automate, and what to escalate.

  • Thrives in ambiguity: You enjoy building systems from scratch in environments where many processes are still undefined.

  • Low ego, team player: You share knowledge freely and care about the success of the broader team.

 

Agency

  • High ownership: You define what needs to be done as often as you execute it. You don't wait for someone to tell you the function has a gap.

  • Systems-first thinking: You focus on eliminating categories of work, not simply resolving tickets faster. You hold yourself and the team accountable to that distinction.

  • Pattern recognition to repeatability: You turn recurring issues into scalable systems, automations, workflows, or documentation that eliminate future occurrences.

  • Deep investigation instincts: You investigate as far as possible before escalating, providing engineering teams with thoughtful, high-context information when collaboration is needed, and you coach the team to do the same.

 

Even if you don’t meet every requirement above, we still encourage you to apply. We care deeply about curiosity, potential, and determination, and we know exceptional people don’t always fit neatly into a checklist.

 

Benefits & Compensation

  • Competitive compensation based on level and experience

    • 100,000€ - 160,000€

  • Significant equity package at a Sequoia-backed startup

  • Health benefits for you and your dependents

  • New MacBook Pro or Linux machine, monitor, keyboard, etc.

  • Opportunity to travel between our Paris and San Francisco offices

  • Regular team events and off-sites

Location

We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.

We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect.

That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call.

Why Dust

The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves.

We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast.

If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk.

Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist.

Learn how we think and work.

jobs.title: Head of ClinOps Data Management RWD/RWE
jobs.description:
À propos de Lifen

Chez Lifen, nous pensons que les données médicales peuvent transformer le système de santé, à condition qu’elles soient accessibles. Mieux les faire circuler, c’est réduire la charge administrative, mieux coordonner les soins et accélérer la recherche clinique.

Depuis 2015, nous développons des solutions qui aident les professionnels de santé à partager les informations médicales et les chercheurs à exploiter des données de santé. Plus de 150 personnes travaillent chez Lifen, depuis nos bureaux et à distance. Nous avons connecté 800 hôpitaux et 150 000 professionnels de santé en France.

Notre équipe

L’équipe Clinical Ops intervient au cœur de nos projets de recherche clinique fondés sur des données de santé. Elle transforme des documents médicaux en données structurées, nécessaires à la constitution de cohortes patients et à la préparation des exports utilisés dans nos projets de recherche.

Aujourd’hui, l’équipe structure environ 100 à 200 cas patients par semaine. Notre ambition : tripler cette capacité dans les 9 prochains mois, tout en maintenant un haut niveau de qualité des données.

Pour y parvenir, nous cherchons une personne capable de reprendre le management de l’équipe, mais surtout de piloter le flux de production, d’anticiper la charge et de porter une démarche d’amélioration continue avec les équipes Produit, IA et Engineering.

C’est un rôle à la croisée du management opérationnel, de la RWD et de l’amélioration de processus.

Ce que tu feras chez nous

Ta première mission sera de reprendre le pilotage de la production des cohortes afin d’en améliorer simultanément la qualité, la capacité de traitement et le niveau d’automatisation.

Concrètement, tu seras amené·e à :

  • Manager et faire grandir l’équipe Clinical Ops, en donnant un cadre clair aux priorités et en organisant l’activité quotidienne.

  • Anticiper la charge et piloter la capacité de production afin de limiter les bottlenecks et de mieux absorber les variations de volume.

  • Construire les outils de pilotage nécessaires pour avoir une vision fine du flux : volumes de patients, capacité de traitement, taux d’erreur, points de blocage et charge de l’équipe.

  • Construire et orchestrer une roadmap d’amélioration continue permettant progressivement d’augmenter la capacité de traitement.

  • Porter cette roadmap auprès des équipes Produit, IA et Engineering : rendre les besoins opérationnels visibles, suivre les livrables R&D et créer le rythme nécessaire pour que les améliorations soient effectivement délivrées.

  • Garantir la qualité des cohortes et contribuer à la préparation des exports de données nécessaires aux projets de recherche.

Ce que nous attendrons de toi

Dans les premiers mois, nous attendrons de toi que tu développes une compréhension très fine du flux Clinical Ops : où se trouvent les blocages, comment évolue la charge et quels leviers permettent réellement d'améliorer la production.

Ton succès se mesurera notamment à ta capacité à mettre en place un pilotage fiable de l’activité, à réduire les erreurs et les bottlenecks et à créer, avec les équipes Produit et R&D, un rythme d’amélioration continue suffisamment soutenu pour accompagner notre changement d’échelle.

À horizon 9 mois, l’objectif est clair : passer d’environ 100–200 à 300–600 cas patients structurés par semaine, sans multiplier les ressources par trois.

Ce que nous recherchons

Must-have

Nous chercherons en priorité trois éléments dans ton parcours :

  • Une expérience réussie en startup ou scale-up, dans un environnement où les process, outils et responsabilités restaient à construire.

  • Une expérience concrète de la Real-World Data / Real-World Evidence, idéalement autour de la constitution ou de l'exploitation de cohortes patients.

  • Un background santé ou scientifique te permettant de comprendre les enjeux liés aux données médicales et à la recherche clinique.

Nous attendons également :

  • Une expérience confirmée de management d’équipe opérationnelle.

  • Une expérience de structuration et de pilotage d’une activité complexe à partir de données et de KPI.

  • Une capacité à passer d’un problème opérationnel très concret à un plan d’amélioration structuré.

  • Une expérience de collaboration étroite avec des équipes Produit, Data/IA ou Engineering.

  • Une capacité à faire avancer une roadmap transverse et à créer de l’accountability autour des livrables.

Nice-to-have

  • Un parcours en data management, biostatistiques, épidémiologie ou dans un domaine scientifique proche.

  • Une expérience de structuration de registres, bases de données de santé ou cohortes RWD.

  • Une familiarité avec les enjeux de recherche clinique et les interactions avec les autorités de santé.

  • Une bonne compréhension des usages de l’IA et de l’ingénierie appliqués aux données de santé.

Ta manière de travailler

Tu as une vraie “just do it mentality” : face à un problème imparfaitement cadré, tu commences par comprendre les faits, tu structures le problème et tu mets rapidement en place les premières solutions.

Tu es particulièrement à l’aise dans les environnements où il faut créer les outils plutôt que simplement les utiliser. Si le dashboard dont tu as besoin pour piloter ton équipe n’existe pas, tu es capable de le définir et de le mettre en place.

Tu es structuré·e et organisé·e, mais pas bureaucratique. Tu sais entrer suffisamment dans le détail du flux pour comprendre les problèmes réels, tout en gardant une vision d’ensemble et en priorisant ce qui aura le plus d’impact.

Enfin, tu sais faire avancer des équipes sur lesquelles tu n’as pas nécessairement d’autorité hiérarchique. Tu rends les problèmes visibles, explicites les priorités et crées le rythme nécessaire pour transformer les décisions en améliorations concrètes.

Nos valeurs

Embrace Complexity — Tu aimes comprendre un flux de données complexe, en identifier les points de rupture et transformer cette complexité en décisions concrètes.

Bienveillance — Tu accompagnes une équipe au quotidien avec exigence, écoute et clarté.

Real Impact — Tu améliores la qualité et la disponibilité des données qui permettent de faire avancer des projets de recherche clinique.

Process de recrutement

Échange de préqualification avec Laura, Talent Acquisition Manager, 30 minutes. Nous faisons connaissance, revenons sur ton parcours, tes attentes et les grandes lignes du poste. C’est aussi le moment de répondre à tes premières questions sur Lifen, l’équipe et le contexte.

Entretien avec le VP Reasearch, 60 minutes. Nous revenons plus en détail sur ton parcours, ton expérience en RWD et en constitution de cohortes, ainsi que sur ton expérience de management et de pilotage d’activités opérationnelles. L’objectif est aussi de comprendre la manière dont tu structures et fais évoluer une organisation dans un environnement en croissance.

Use Case avec des membres des équipes Clinical Ops et Produit, 60 minutes. À partir de situations concrètes, nous échangeons sur ta manière de structurer une cohorte RWD, d’analyser des problématiques opérationnelles et de construire des plans d’amélioration. Ce sera également l’occasion d’aborder la manière dont tu gères les enjeux humains et la collaboration avec des équipes transverses.

Cultural alignment avec deux membres de Lifen, 45 minutes en visio. Ce temps permettra d’échanger sur ta façon de travailler, ton niveau d’autonomie, la collaboration au quotidien et l’adéquation avec nos valeurs.

Compensation: €65K – €75K

At Gigaton, we’re on a mission to cut gigatonnes of carbon emissions from the world’s biggest emitting industries (like cement, steel and glass), by building autonomous AI control and optimisation systems that learn and leverage the physics of manufacturing. Our products run heavy industrial plants more efficiently, more stably, and with lower emissions in real time - laying the foundation for the next industrial revolution.

We are a team of scientists, engineers, builders, and operators who love hard problems, have high standards, and want to make change happen in the physical world. We care about deep tech, but we care even more about whether it delivers cost and carbon impact in a live plant, with real people, under real constraints.

With Gigaton, you’ll solve really tough problems in places few people ever get close to, and build something that actually helps the planet. Are you up for the challenge?

About the role

We're looking for a Director of Deployment to lead our Solutions team, the engineers who get our product live in industrial customers' plants, and to make every deployment faster, better and more reliable than the last.

You'll be accountable for every deployment we run, and be the senior escalation route, for our team and our customers, when something gets stuck.

This is a new role, and a leadership role, but a hands-on one. You'll coach our solutions engineers and leaders as they own deployments and customer relationships themselves, and step in yourself when a plant needs it. You'll work with Product, Machine Learning and Engineering to decide what goes back into the core product, so every plant is faster than the last.

What will this role achieve?

The goal: Take Gigaton from 9 plants live to 50 by the end of 2027, with every new plant going from signed contract to the end of evaluation in 8 weeks.

Outcome – 50 plants live. You've taken us from 9 plants to 50 by 31 December 2027, across our customers worldwide. You've planned how many engineers we need and which teams new joiners go into, tracked the health of the whole portfolio every week, and stepped in early when a deployment started to drift.

Outcome – 8 weeks from contract to results. Today a plant takes about six months to reach evaluation. You've cut that to 8 weeks end to end, and published the numbers that prove it. You've done it by turning repeated human work and customer-specific work into product, built with Product and Engineering. Each plant now needs half the people it did when you joined.

Outcome – a grip on results. Before we start, every plant has agreed with us what success looks like and whose data counts. You've balanced the need to hit our timelines with the need to pass evaluations, pausing a plant that isn't ready rather than letting it fail, so every evaluation has passed first time. When something has gone wrong, you've found the root cause fast and fixed it, so we only make each mistake once.

Outcome – a team of superstars that keeps growing. You've designed the team that delivers 50 plants and grown it to the size your design needs, hiring people who raise our bar. You've coached it actively: your leaders run high-performing teams, every engineer is autonomous, happy and smashing it for our customers, and everyone in Solutions can name what they've got better at because of you. We haven't lost anyone we wanted to keep.

Outcome – customers who trust us at every level. Every plant has a clear owner, and an escalation route that solves problems before they reach our exec team. You've built a clean handover from Sales and a voice for Deployment in which plants we take on.

Outcome – post-sales solved. With our sales leader, you've set up how we run every plant after evaluation, and it works, with clear responsibilities mapped out. Model upkeep, support and retraining are handled. Expansion contracts and upsells run through the same model: each one has a clear owner, and we spot opportunities before the customer raises them.

What a great fit looks like

  • You have deployed early AI product into business customers, hands-on and alongside engineers. You worked out what would create value and decided what was worth building. Not onboarding customers onto a product that was already finished.

  • You have turned bespoke work into repeatable product. You decided which customer-specific features and fixes belonged in the core product, and you can show the numbers: deployments that got faster, with fewer people, while volume grew.

  • You have earned the trust of customer leaders, from site head up to executive level, been their escalation point and unblocked hard problems. You're credible because you've built and shipped.

  • You have grown a delivery team and made the decisions that came with it, including hiring and performance management. You've designed the team's structure as it grew.

  • You're a coach who was recently a quarterback. You can still step in, but you know you'll have more impact by building a team that doesn't need you to.

  • You agree what success means with a customer before you start, and you prove it with numbers.

  • You notice early signs of trouble and raise them with urgency, and you use judgement to tell what needs action and what doesn't.

  • You're happy to travel to our plants worldwide, about a quarter of the time and more in your first few months: to build relationships with customer leaders, coach your team on site and learn how our plants run.

You'll excel if

  • You have managed managers, or grown an engineer into a team lead.

  • You have worked in a forward-deployed or deployment strategist model, where small teams embed with customers.

  • You have set up post-sales or account management for a B2B product.

  • You have deployed software into physical operations: plants, factories, utilities, energy assets or similar.

  • You care about decarbonising energy intensive industries.

Details

  • Reports to: Noah Miller, COO

  • Team: our Solutions team of solutions engineers and two team leads, which you'll lead and grow

  • Location: London, at least 2 days a week in the office, with about 25% travel to customer plants

  • Visa sponsorship: available if required

💡 You are not expected to check every box, and we’d love to hear from you even if your experience isn’t an exact match.

We’re building a team that reflects the world we want to change. Our people come from different countries, cultures and experiences, and we think that’s one of our biggest strengths.

We’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels safe, respected and celebrated. No matter your background, if you’re excited by what we do, we want to hear from you.

The interview process - subject to change

We aim to go from first call to offer in three weeks.

  1. First call with our Talent team (30 minutes)

  2. Interview with Noah, our COO, walking through your career (60 minutes)

  3. Work sample day. We share real data from one of our plants. You spend 30 minutes with two of our team leads, then present how you'd run the deployment and how you'd shape the team for 50 plants. This includes a conversation about how you lead people. We'll give you the background you need beforehand.

  4. Operating Principles interview with a panel from across Gigaton

  5. Final interview with Josh, our CEO

  6. References, then an offer

We believe hiring is a two-way process. Just as we’ll reference-check candidates before making a final offer, we encourage you to reference-check us by chatting to team members you haven’t yet met. Ask anything. We’ll answer with Concrete Honesty.

Once interviews are done, we’ll move quickly to a decision, and we’re always happy to give feedback at any stage.

Our Operating Principles

↗️ Go Gig or Go Home: High Bar, All In. What we do matters to humanity, to our customers and to each other. We hold ourselves to an extraordinarily high bar and bring the urgency this mission requires.

jobs.title: Embedded Engineer
jobs.description:
Accelerating embodied AGI.

The next ten years of AI will not be won in software. They will be won in the physical world: in factories, hospitals, kitchens, fields, and homes. The companies that own that data will own the century.

MicroAGI is building it. We are a data research and deployment lab. Atlas captures the manual work inside Europe’s industrial champions, trains foundation models on it, and deploys the right robot onto the floor, with no teleoperation and no interruption to the line. Shift records how physical work actually happens and turns it into training-ready data.

We were founded by former Formula 1 engineers from Red Bull Racing and Mercedes, together with a researcher from the Alan Turing Institute. Our $55M seed round, the largest in German history, was led by Hummingbird with Northzone, LocalGlobe, Village Global, and redalpine. We are based in Munich, with our research centre in Zürich and teams in London, New York, and Istanbul. We are now building the engineering and research teams that will take Atlas into new industries.

Our models learn from data captured in the physical world, by hardware we design and build ourselves. As Embedded Engineer, you will own the firmware that runs on that hardware, from the first register write to the moment data leaves the device, so that what reaches our ML team is clean, synchronized, and trustworthy.

What You Will Do

  • Write and own the firmware for our data-capture hardware: sensors, motion-capture rigs, custom IoT setups, and prototype robots.

  • Build real-time data acquisition: drivers, DMA, buffering, and streaming from many sensors at once without dropping a sample.

  • Solve multi-sensor synchronization, calibration, and time-stamping so every data point lines up across devices and modalities.

  • Bring up new boards with our Electrical Engineer and turn fresh hardware into working devices fast.

  • Build the path from device to dataset: communication protocols, on-device logging, and handoff into our data pipeline.

  • Work shoulder to shoulder with ML engineers. Your firmware decides what their training data looks like, and a timing bug can quietly ruin months of data.

  • Make firmware reliable in the field: testing, OTA updates, error handling, and diagnostics that tell us what went wrong.

Requirements

  • Up to 5 years writing production firmware for embedded or IoT systems.

  • Strong C/C++, experience with an RTOS (FreeRTOS, Zephyr, or similar), and deep familiarity with microcontrollers (STM32, ESP32, NXP, or similar).

  • Hands-on experience with peripheral interfaces and protocols: SPI, I2C, UART, USB, BLE, CAN, or similar.

  • Experience integrating sensors in firmware: IMUs, cameras, depth sensors, force sensors, or similar.

  • A strong understanding of how firmware decisions affect data quality, especially for EMG/EEG sensing: ADC configuration, sample rate, jitter, filtering, and buffering. You know that a great model on a noisy signal still loses to a decent model on a clean one, and you write code accordingly.

  • Comfortable debugging at the hardware boundary with a logic analyzer, oscilloscope, and debugger.

  • Genuinely curious about ML: you read papers, you have trained at least one model end to end, and you understand that dataset quality beats model architecture choice.

  • High agency: you don't wait to be told what to do. You are comfortable in 0-to-1 ambiguity, where the spec is "figure out what the spec should be".

  • Discreet: you handle confidential hardware roadmaps and customer data with care.

  • Fluent in English. German is a plus.

Nice to Have

  • A background in robotics, motion capture, or wearable devices.

  • Experience with real-time or hard-deadline systems: audio, video sync, or robotic control loops.

  • Experience with embedded Linux, time-sync protocols (PTP or similar), or low-power design.

  • Familiarity with ML training pipelines. Even if you don't run them, you can read a training script.

  • Open-source firmware contributions.

  • Experience taking firmware from prototype to small-batch production: test fixtures, provisioning, and certification support.

Who Will Thrive at MicroAGI

Everyone we hire is assessed on the same four traits:

  • Mission and vision: you care about what we are building and why it matters, and your past choices show it.

  • Intensity: you work at a pace that matches the size of the opportunity, and you sustain it.

  • Entrepreneurial: you start things nobody asked for, and you finish them.

  • Raw IQ: you learn fast, reason from first principles, and get sharper when the problem changes.

This is for you if:

  • You would rather own a problem end to end than wait for a spec.

  • You use AI every day, and you can tell a correct answer from a plausible one.

  • You want to work in person, in the office, with people who are very good at what they do.

This is not for you if:

  • You are looking for a predictable 9-to-5.

  • You would forward output you cannot explain.

  • "That’s not my job" feels like a reasonable answer.

How We Hire

We read every application and reply within five working days.

  1. Talent Screen (30 min): a first conversation, both ways.

  2. Technical or Functional Interview (60 min): how you think when the problem changes.

  3. Your Work (60 min): bring something you are proud of and walk us through it.

  4. Leadership (30 min): a conversation with our CEO.

  5. Coworking Day (engineering and research roles): a day building with the team on a real problem.

Then a decision, usually within a few days.

Pay Transparency

Compensation includes base salary and equity. The salary range for this role is shown on this posting.

What We Offer

  • Agency: real ownership from day one, and decisions that actually matter.

  • Freedom: to choose how you solve the problem, without layers of approval.

  • A seat on a rocketship: one of Europe’s fastest-growing deep-tech companies, at the earliest stage.

  • Free food and drinks in the office.

Equal Opportunity

MicroAGI welcomes applications from everyone. We assess candidates on their work and potential, regardless of ethnic origin, gender, religion or belief, disability, age, or sexual identity.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager (f/m/x)
jobs.description:
Your Mission

This is a company built for growth, not comfort.

When you join exmox, you're stepping onto a global, highly competitive playing field, solving real problems in environments that push you beyond your comfort zone.

We build high-performing consumer products in one of the most competitive industries there is: mobile gaming, leading one of its largest innovations, a rewarded user engagement and acquisition platform that helps publishers acquire and retain players through rewarding experiences.

Senior Product Manager (f/m/x) isn't just about shipping features, it's about building products that perform. Product at exmox means understanding the bigger business picture, considering cross-functional impact across Engineering, Data, Marketing, and Operations, and turning strategy into product decisions that create real value, knowing every change you ship affects millions of users. At exmox, we're also embracing AI as part of how we work, not just what we build. We use AI tools to work smarter, cut down on repetitive tasks and spend our time where it actually moves the needle. If that mindset speaks to you, you'll fit right in.

If you're energized by dynamic markets, complex products, and the challenge of building products that perform at scale, we want to hear from you.

What You’ll Own:

  • Own one of exmox's highest-impact product domains end-to-end, shaping the reward economy through payout thresholds, tiering, bonuses, promotions, and other key levers that drive profitability.
  • Drive activation, retention, and long-term engagement through onboarding experiences, streaks, quests, progression systems, reactivation flows, and other lifecycle initiatives.
  • Take new growth opportunities from first hypothesis to go/no-go decision, across product, market expansion, partnerships, and distribution.
  • Lead a high-quality experimentation process by defining hypotheses, designing statistically sound A/B tests, interpreting results, and making data-driven product decisions.
  • Partner closely with your dedicated Data Analyst to uncover opportunities, validate assumptions, and continuously improve product performance.
  • Work with Engineering, Design, Commercial, User Acquisition, Customer Support, Fraud, and Leadership to align priorities and deliver impactful product improvements.
  • Represent your product domain directly to leadership, using data, customer insights, and business context to influence strategic decisions.

What Success Looks Like:

  • You take ownership quickly: Within your first months, you've become the trusted owner of a critical product domain, confidently driving priorities, making decisions, and reducing dependency on leadership.
  • Growth metrics measurably improve: Your product strategy and experimentation drive meaningful improvements in activation, retention, and long-term user profitability.
  • Product decisions are driven by data: Experiments, user insights, and product analytics provide clear evidence to prioritize opportunities, validate ideas, and confidently decide what to scale - or stop.
  • Cross-functional teams are aligned around outcomes: You partner closely with Engineering, Design, Data, Commercial, and User Acquisition to deliver product improvements that balance user value with business impact.
  • You turn ambitious ideas into scalable growth: Through structured experimentation, clear prioritization, and continuous optimization, you build product experiences that become repeatable growth levers for the business.
  • You outgrow the role: We are hiring for the ceiling, not just the opening. This role is scoped to grow - mentoring other product managers first, and leading a product team as we scale, if that is the direction you want to take.

What You Bring

  • Experienced: You bring 5+ years of Product Management experience in consumer-facing digital products, ideally within mobile apps, gaming, marketplaces, subscriptions, ad-tech, fintech, or other high-growth B2C businesses. You have owned consumer product at scale - hundreds of thousands of monthly active users or more.
  • Business-Oriented: You understand that product decisions are business decisions. You're comfortable balancing user needs, commercial objectives, and technical constraints to maximize long-term value.
  • Fluent in Incentives: You have a real feel for why people come back and what makes a reward feel worth the effort. You have designed incentive, reward or progression mechanics and calibrated them so they motivate without eroding margin.
  • Experimentation-Driven: You have extensive experience running A/B tests, defining hypotheses, interpreting data, and making evidence-based product decisions. Statistical thinking comes naturally to you.
  • Data-Literate: You're comfortable working with product metrics and collaborating closely with analysts to uncover insights, measure success, and prioritize opportunities.
  • Strategic & Hands-on: You enjoy defining product strategy while remaining deeply involved in execution - from writing specifications and refining solutions to reviewing experiment results and driving delivery.
  • Collaborative: You build strong partnerships across Product, Engineering, Design, Analytics, Marketing, Commercial, and Leadership, bringing people together around clear product goals.
  • Intellectually Honest: You're comfortable working in ambiguity, take ownership without waiting for direction, and thrive in fast-moving environments where priorities evolve quickly. You also kill your own ideas when the data says so - being wrong early is cheaper than being right late.

How We Win

  • Speed is the feature. Speed beats rocket science. We move fast, test fast, and multiply our pace with AI, because action creates information and small wins compound. A fast failure is a lesson we learn from, a slow one is a problem we can't afford.
  • Focus on the essential. Done is better than perfect. We stay focused on what actually moves us forward and protect people's time from anything that doesn't. We're direct in how we communicate too, no rambling, no unnecessary detail.
  • See it. Own it. Solve it. The first to see it is best placed to fix it. We're not a place for comfort, we're a place for doers. "Not my job" isn't in our vocabulary, if you spot something, you help make sure it gets solved.
  • Respect others. Trust multiplies. Respect is non-negotiable. We disagree with ideas, never with people. Trust here is built the same way it is anywhere, through consistency, a thank you, a moment of listening, and owning your mistakes.
  • Perks that help you focus on what matters. Transport subsidy, learning budget, wellness and gym, workation, bi-weekly team lunches, and more. The perks are great, but the real reason people join and stay is the challenge, the ownership, and the drive to win together.
